body.statement: For each fixed \(c>0\) and \(v\in\{\mathrm w,+\}\), the nonempty fiber \(\{\Delta:(\log c,\Delta)\in\Theta_v(P)\}\) is an interval whose infimum and supremum equal the optimal values of the two linear semidefinite programs over \(\mathcal F_c^v(P,\Delta)\). Endpoint inclusion is equivalent to the separate feasibility tests in \(\mathrm{def{:}endpoint\text{-}attainment\text{-}test}\); neither inclusion is inferred from closed PSD constraints alone.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(c>0\), \(v\in\{\mathrm w,+\}\), and a law \(P\) satisfying \(\mathrm{ass{:}positive\text{-}observed\text{-}cells}\), and suppose
\[
 I_v(P,c)=\{d:(\log c,d)\in\Theta_v(P)\}
\]
is nonempty.  Write \(z_{\mathrm w}=(m,a,b)\), \(z_+=(m,a,b,t)\), and
\[
 \mathcal G_v(P,c)=\{(z_v,d):z_v\in\mathcal F_c^v(P,d)\}. \tag{1}
\]
For fixed \(P,c\), every entry of \(H_s,K_s\), and, for \(v=+\), \(R_s\), is affine in \(z_v\); the cell restrictions are affine equalities; and the APE restriction is
\[
 d=\sum_{s\in S}L_{m_s}(N_c). \tag{2}
\]
If \(M_0,M_1\succeq0\) and \(0\le\lambda\le1\), then for every vector \(q\),
\[
 q^{\mathsf T}\{\lambda M_0+(1-\lambda)M_1\}q
 =\lambda q^{\mathsf T}M_0q+(1-\lambda)q^{\mathsf T}M_1q\ge0. \tag{3}
\]
Thus every PSD constraint is convex and \(\mathcal G_v(P,c)\) is convex.  Its linear projection onto \(d\) is therefore an interval.  By \(\mathrm{thm{:}exact\text{-}feedback\text{-}cone}\), this projection equals \(I_v(P,c)\), so it is the model-defined sharp fiber and not an outer approximation.

The sharp universal geometry in \(\mathrm{thm{:}sharp\text{-}slope\text{-}ape\text{-}envelope}\) gives the stronger sign-sensitive containment
\[
 I_v(P,c)\subseteq
 \begin{cases}
 (0,(\sqrt c-1)/(\sqrt c+1)],&c>1,\\
 [-(1-\sqrt c)/(1+\sqrt c),0),&0<c<1,\\
 \{0\},&c=1.
 \end{cases} \tag{4}
\]
This is an outer envelope for a fixed observed law \(P\), although it is sharp when laws are allowed to vary.  In particular, the nonempty interval \(I_v(P,c)\) is bounded and has finite infimum and supremum.

The two finite-dimensional programs are explicitly
\[
 \underline V_v(P,c)=\inf_{d,z_v}\{d:z_v\in\mathcal F_c^v(P,d)\},
 \qquad
 \overline V_v(P,c)=\sup_{d,z_v}\{d:z_v\in\mathcal F_c^v(P,d)\}. \tag{5}
\]
Their objectives are linear, their equalities are affine, and their matrix inequalities are affine PSD constraints, so they are linear semidefinite programs.  Exactness gives
\[
 \underline V_v(P,c)=\inf I_v(P,c)=L_c^v(P),
 \qquad
 \overline V_v(P,c)=\sup I_v(P,c)=U_c^v(P). \tag{6}
\]
They are sharp endpoint values because \(I_v(P,c)\) is the independently defined legal fiber.

For endpoint inclusion, the lower value belongs to the model fiber exactly when
\((\log c,L_c^v(P))\in\Theta_v(P)\).  Applying the exact cone equivalence at this particular value yields
\[
 L_c^v(P)\in I_v(P,c)
 \Longleftrightarrow
 \mathcal F_c^v(P,L_c^v(P))\ne\varnothing. \tag{7}
\]
Likewise,
\[
 U_c^v(P)\in I_v(P,c)
 \Longleftrightarrow
 \mathcal F_c^v(P,U_c^v(P))\ne\varnothing. \tag{8}
\]
These are the two separate tests in \(\mathrm{def{:}endpoint\text{-}attainment\text{-}test}\).

Closedness of the matrix cones alone cannot replace (7)--(8), because linear projection need not preserve closedness.  For example,
\[
 \mathcal C=\left\{(x,y):
 \begin{bmatrix}x&1\\1&y\end{bmatrix}\succeq0\right\}
\]
is closed, while its projection onto the \(x\)-coordinate is \((0,\infty)\): PSD is equivalent to \(x\ge0\), \(y\ge0\), and \(xy\ge1\).  Thus neither endpoint inclusion follows merely from the closed PSD constraints.  Equations (1)--(8) prove all assertions.
body.justification: The exact cone makes the endpoint programs sharp, while the universal envelope gives finite sign-sensitive geometry and the separate feasibility tests handle nonattainment.
body.gap: A numerical grid endpoint does not reveal whether the model fiber is open, closed, or half-open at that value.
body.consumer: Applied work can report endpoint values, their inclusion flags, and the universal benchmark \(|\Delta|\le\tanh(|\theta|/4)\).
